doc_title: P3 — Logstash IOT-PIPELINE-01 dead letter queue depth exceeded threshold
text:
INCIDENT RECORD INC-0052001
Priority: P3 | Status: Resolved | Resolution time: 1h 45min

DESCRIPTION
Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) depth on Logstash node logstash-02 exceeded the monitoring threshold of 1,000 events at 14:22 UTC on 2024-10-08. Impacted pipeline: IOT-PIPELINE-01 (apex_operational_telemetry). Root cause: 47 sensor readings from Plant-Barcelona-3 were transmitted with a malformed JSON payload (missing required field asset_type). Logstash could not validate schema and routed events to DLQ. No data loss: DLQ events were replayed after schema fix.

ROOT CAUSE
Firmware update deployed to Barcelona sensor cluster (firmware 3.3 → 3.4) on 2024-10-07 introduced a breaking change in the JSON serialization of the asset_type enum field — it was serialized as an integer enum index instead of the string value. The Logstash grok filter expected string. Fix: updated grok pattern in IOT-PIPELINE-01 to accept both integer and string formats for asset_type.

RESOLUTION
14:22 — DLQ alert fired, on-call engineer notified.
14:38 — Root cause identified (Barcelona firmware mismatch).
14:55 — Logstash filter updated and deployed to all 3 nodes (rolling restart).
15:00 — DLQ replayed: 47 events successfully re-processed and indexed.
16:07 — DLQ depth confirmed 0, monitoring alert cleared.

ACTIONS
PLAT-4701: Add firmware version field to IoT event schema; alert if mismatch detected.
PLAT-4702: Pre-production Logstash filter testing required for all firmware updates.

doc_title: P2 — Jina CLIP v2 inference endpoint OOM on ML node, multimodal search unavailable 3h
text:
INCIDENT RECORD INC-0052109
Priority: P2 | Status: Resolved | Resolution time: 3h 12min

DESCRIPTION
The jina-clip-v2 inference endpoint on ml-01 ran out of GPU memory (OOM) at 09:14 UTC on 2024-11-01, causing all multimodal searches against apex_multimodal_assets to return 503 errors. The inference endpoint for jina-v3-multilingual on the same node was unaffected. Root cause: a batch embedding job initiated by the pharma QC team processed 1,247 chromatography chart images in a single request with batch_size=128, exhausting the 40 GB A100 VRAM.

TECHNICAL DETAILS
jina-clip-v2 model VRAM requirements: base model 8.2 GB + 512 MB per concurrent inference worker + input batch memory. With batch_size=128 and average image resolution 1024x1024 RGB: input tensor = 128 * 3 * 1024 * 1024 * 4 bytes = 1.6 GB per batch. At 5 concurrent workers (default): 5 * (8.2 + 0.5 + 1.6) = 51.5 GB — exceeds 40 GB VRAM.

RESOLUTION
09:14 — OOM detected, endpoint auto-restarted (k8s liveness probe).
09:31 — Auto-restart failed (OOM on restart due to residual batch job).
09:45 — Manual pod kill and restart with reduced max_batch_size=32.
10:22 — Endpoint healthy. Batch job resubmitted in 50-document chunks.
12:26 — All 1,247 images embedded successfully.

PREVENTIVE ACTIONS
PLAT-4750: Set hard limit max_batch_size=32 for jina-clip-v2 endpoint config.
PLAT-4751: Add GPU memory utilization to Kibana ML node dashboard.
PLAT-4752: Batch embedding jobs > 100 documents require approval via JIRA ticket.

doc_title: P1 — apex_security_acls index corruption after partial shard failure
text:
INCIDENT RECORD INC-0052340
Priority: P1 | Status: Resolved | Resolution time: 6h 55min

DESCRIPTION
At 22:03 UTC on 2024-11-15, data node es-data-prod-03 experienced an NVMe SSD controller failure. The node was removed from the cluster automatically. Three primary shards were reassigned to other nodes. One shard — shard 2 of apex_security_acls — failed to reassign due to insufficient disk space on remaining hot nodes (a pre-existing disk capacity issue). The shard remained unassigned (RED status). During the 6h55min RED period, all API requests checking DLS filters against apex_security_acls failed with 503, causing AFDS fraud scoring to reject all DLS-filtered queries and fall back to fail-open (no DLS applied — all documents visible to all authenticated roles).

IMPACT
During the outage window, the following DLS filters were NOT enforced: ROLE-SALES (customers of other account managers visible), ROLE-DS-ANON (all financial transactions visible without anonymization). No evidence of actual unauthorized data access during this window (access logs reviewed by CISO team — all queries originated from automated AFDS pipelines, not human users). However, a regulatory notification assessment was conducted — concluded below DSGVO Art. 33 notification threshold (no actual unauthorized disclosure confirmed).

RESOLUTION
22:03 — Alert: cluster RED, apex_security_acls shard unassigned.
22:18 — es-data-prod-03 confirmed hardware failure, decommissioned.
22:45 — Attempted manual shard allocation to warm nodes — blocked by index tier routing setting (hot-only).
23:15 — Temporarily overrode tier routing: PUT apex_security_acls/_settings {"index.routing.allocation.require._tier": null}.
23:22 — Shard allocated to es-data-prod-05. Data recovery from replica: complete (100% of documents recovered).
04:58 — New hot node es-data-prod-07 provisioned (48h SLA from infra team). Shard migrated back to hot tier.

PREVENTIVE ACTIONS
PLAT-4800: apex_security_acls index must have 2 replicas (currently 1) — any single node failure must not cause RED status.
PLAT-4801: DLS failure mode: when apex_security_acls is unavailable, AFDS must DENY-ALL (fail-closed) not fail-open.
PLAT-4802: Hot tier disk utilization alert at 70% (currently 80%).
PLAT-4803: Replace es-data-prod-03 NVMe SSD — also audit all other nodes manufactured before 2022.

doc_title: Apex Conglomerate — Network Architecture Overview v3.2
text:
NETWORK ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW v3.2

1. NETWORK TOPOLOGY
The Apex Conglomerate production network follows a defense-in-depth architecture across two primary datacenters (Frankfurt, Amsterdam DR) with a hub-and-spoke WAN connecting 14 office locations across Europe.

FRANKFURT DATACENTER (PRIMARY)
Physical: 2x Cisco Nexus 9000 core switches (active/active ECMP), 4x Cisco Nexus 5000 distribution switches, 48x Cisco Catalyst 9000 access switches. Total capacity: 100 Gbps core uplinks, 25 Gbps inter-tier links, 10 Gbps to server NICs.
WAN: 2x 10 Gbps MPLS circuits (primary: Deutsche Telekom; backup: Colt) + 4x 1 Gbps SD-WAN overlays for branch connectivity.

VLAN SEGMENTATION
VLAN 10 — Management: BMC/IPMI/iDRAC interfaces, jump hosts, network equipment management. Firewall: strict whitelist, no internet access.
VLAN 100 — Production servers (frontend tier): load balancers (HAProxy, F5), reverse proxies, API gateways. DMZ segment, internet-facing.
VLAN 200 — Production servers (application tier): all application servers, ES coordinating nodes, AFDS scoring service. No direct internet access.
VLAN 300 — Production servers (data tier): ES data nodes (hot/warm/cold), ML nodes, Kafka brokers. Isolated from frontend. Strict firewall rules.
VLAN 400 — IoT network: dedicated isolated segment for MQTT broker and IoT edge nodes. No routing to production VLANs except via controlled MQTT gateway.
VLAN 500 — Kubernetes: pod/service CIDR (10.96.0.0/12), MetalLB address pool. Calico CNI with NetworkPolicy enforcement.
VLAN 600 — Corporate: employee workstations, VDI. No direct access to data tier VLANs.
VLAN 700 — DR replication: cross-datacenter CCR and backup traffic only. Encrypted (IPSec).

FIREWALL RULES (key rules)
ES data nodes → ES coordinating nodes: TCP 9200 (REST) and 9300 (transport). Bidirectional.
AFDS scoring service → ES coordinating: TCP 9200 only.
Logstash → ES coordinating: TCP 9200 only.
IoT MQTT gateway → Kafka: TCP 9092 (SASL/SSL). Kafka → Logstash: TCP 9092.
All nodes → Vault: TCP 8200 (HTTPS). Vault → Azure AD: TCP 443.
Management VLAN → all: SSH TCP 22, IPMI UDP 623. All other traffic blocked.

doc_title: Apex Conglomerate — Network Architecture Overview v3.2
text:
2. ZERO TRUST NETWORK ARCHITECTURE

Following CISO directive SEC-POL-2023-04, Apex is implementing Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) across all production services. Current state (2024) and target state (2025):

CURRENT STATE: Perimeter-based security with VPN for remote access. Service-to-service communication within trusted VLANs relies on network-level trust. API keys required for Elasticsearch access but no mutual authentication for intra-VLAN service calls.

TARGET STATE (2025): Full ZTNA implementation. All service-to-service calls require: mutual TLS with short-lived certificates (Vault PKI, 24h TTL); identity-based authorization via SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity; no implicit trust based on network location — every request authenticated regardless of VLAN.

IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP
Phase 1 (Q1 2025 — COMPLETE): Implement mTLS for all Elasticsearch API communications (intra-cluster transport already uses mTLS; adding mTLS for Logstash-to-ES and AFDS-to-ES). See CHG-0031300.
Phase 2 (Q2 2025): Deploy HashiCorp Consul service mesh for AFDS, Logstash, Kafka. Service discovery replaces hardcoded IP addresses.
Phase 3 (Q3 2025): SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity rollout across all Kubernetes pods.
Phase 4 (Q4 2025): Retire legacy VPN. Replace with Cloudflare Access ZTNA (EU data processing agreement in place).

3. DNS ARCHITECTURE
Internal DNS: CoreDNS on Kubernetes (service discovery), Infoblox DDI for infrastructure DNS. Key records:
es-api.apex.internal → HAProxy VIP 10.10.200.50 (coordinating nodes, port 9200)
kibana.apex.internal → HAProxy VIP 10.10.200.51 (Kibana cluster, port 5601)
kafka.apex.internal → CNAME round-robin to 3 broker IPs (10.10.300.21, .22, .23)
vault.apex.internal → Vault active node (10.10.200.60, auto-updated by Vault agent)
mqtt.apex.internal → Mosquitto VIP 10.10.400.10

doc_title: Apex Conglomerate — Kubernetes Platform Architecture v2.5 (k8s-es-prod)
text:
KUBERNETES PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE v2.5 — k8s-es-prod

1. CLUSTER SPECIFICATIONS
Cluster name: k8s-es-prod
Kubernetes version: 1.29.3 (upgraded quarterly)
Cluster type: Bare-metal on VMware vSphere 8 (Tanzu Kubernetes Grid)
CNI: Calico 3.27 (NetworkPolicy enforcement, BGP routing to physical switches)
CSI: VMware vSphere CSI 3.1 (NVMe storage classes for ES data nodes, HDD for warm tier)
Load balancer: MetalLB 0.13 (BGP mode, 10.10.100.0/24 address pool)
Ingress: NGINX Ingress Controller 1.9 (deployed in separate ingress namespace)
GitOps: ArgoCD 2.9 (all manifests in git repo ops-platform/k8s-es-prod/)

NODE POOL LAYOUT
master-pool: 3 nodes (k8s-master-01/02/03) — 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM. Control plane only, tainted NoSchedule for workloads.
es-hot-pool: 6 nodes (k8s-es-hot-01 through 06) — 32 vCPU, 128 GB RAM, 4 TB NVMe x2 (RAID-0 per node). Node label: apex/tier=hot.
es-ml-pool: 2 nodes (k8s-es-ml-01/02) — 64 vCPU, 256 GB RAM, 2x NVIDIA A100 40GB. Node label: apex/tier=ml. GPU operator: NVIDIA GPU Operator 23.9.
es-warm-pool: 2 nodes (k8s-es-warm-01/02) — 16 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 16 TB HDD. Node label: apex/tier=warm.
es-cold-pool: 2 nodes (k8s-es-cold-01/02) — 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, MinIO S3 mount (32 TB). Node label: apex/tier=cold.
es-coord-pool: 2 nodes (k8s-es-coord-01/02) — 16 vCPU, 64 GB RAM. Coordinating + Kibana. Node label: apex/tier=coordinating.
infra-pool: 4 nodes (k8s-infra-01 through 04) — 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM. Logstash, Kafka, Vault agent, monitoring.

2. ECK (ELASTIC CLOUD ON KUBERNETES) CONFIGURATION
ECK operator version: 2.9.0
Deployed via ArgoCD app: argocd/apps/eck-operator.yaml
ECK manages: Elasticsearch cluster (es-prod), Kibana instances (kibana-prod), APM Server (apm-prod), Elastic Agent (agent-prod fleet).
Key ECK custom resources:
- Elasticsearch CR: spec.nodeSets defines 6 node pools matching physical layout above. Pod disruption budgets: master (minAvailable: 2), hot-data (minAvailable: 4), ML (minAvailable: 1).
- Kibana CR: 3 replicas, resource limits 4 CPU / 16 Gi RAM, ingress via NGINX with Azure AD SAML SSO.
- Agent CR: DaemonSet on all nodes (Filebeat, Metricbeat for cluster monitoring).

doc_title: Apex Conglomerate — Disaster Recovery Architecture v2.0
text:
DISASTER RECOVERY ARCHITECTURE v2.0

1. DR STRATEGY AND OBJECTIVES
Apex Conglomerate operates a Warm Standby DR model for the Elasticsearch platform, with Cross-Cluster Replication (CCR) providing near-real-time data synchronization between the Frankfurt primary cluster (es-prod) and the Amsterdam DR cluster (es-dr).

Recovery Objectives:
- Tier 1 indices (apex_financial_transactions, apex_customer_360, apex_customer_interactions, apex_operational_telemetry, apex_pharma_batches): RTO = 30 minutes, RPO = 30 seconds
- Tier 2 indices (apex_knowledge_graph, apex_policy_vault, apex_it_knowledge_base, apex_technical_docs, apex_security_acls): RTO = 4 hours, RPO = 1 hour (scheduled snapshot-based replication)
- Tier 3 indices (apex_multimodal_assets, apex_unstructured_vault): RTO = 24 hours, RPO = 24 hours (daily snapshot)

2. CROSS-CLUSTER REPLICATION (CCR) CONFIGURATION
CCR mode: Uni-directional (Frankfurt leader → Amsterdam follower). Bidirectional CCR considered but rejected: risk of split-brain during partial network partition.
CCR polling interval: 100ms (Tier 1 indices). Results in typical lag < 5 seconds under normal load. Worst-case observed lag: 28 seconds during Frankfurt peak indexing (Friday 18:00-19:00 CET).
CCR auto-follow pattern: apex_financial_transactions-*, apex_customer_360-*, apex_customer_interactions-*, apex_operational_telemetry-*, apex_pharma_batches-* (captures ILM-managed rollover indices automatically).
CCR monitoring: custom Kibana dashboard (https://kibana.apex.dr/dashboard/ccr-lag) showing per-index replication lag in seconds. Alert: lag > 60 seconds triggers P3 alert; lag > 300 seconds triggers P2.

3. AMSTERDAM DR CLUSTER SPECIFICATION
Cluster: es-dr (Amsterdam, separate VMware vSphere cluster hosted in AMS datacenter)
Nodes: 2x master-eligible (8 vCPU, 32 GB), 4x data hot (16 vCPU, 64 GB, 2 TB NVMe), 1x ML node (32 vCPU, 128 GB, NVIDIA A100 — for inference during DR), 1x coordinating (8 vCPU, 32 GB), 2x Kibana (4 vCPU, 16 GB)
Total storage: 8 TB hot (lower capacity than Frankfurt — DR cluster sized at 60% of primary)
Network: 10 Gbps dedicated MPLS circuit Frankfurt → Amsterdam (primary CCR path). 1 Gbps IPSec backup tunnel (VPN).

4. SNAPSHOT STRATEGY
Repository: MinIO S3-compatible (apex-snapshots bucket, Frankfurt MinIO cluster for primary snapshots; replicated to Amsterdam MinIO for DR copy).
Automated snapshots via Snapshot Lifecycle Management (SLM):
- Tier 1 indices: every 6 hours, retain 28 snapshots (7 days x 4/day)
- Tier 2 indices: daily at 01:00 UTC, retain 30 snapshots
- Tier 3 indices: weekly Sunday 02:00 UTC, retain 12 snapshots
Snapshot encryption: AES-256, keys managed by Vault. Snapshot verification: weekly restore test to isolated test cluster (k8s-es-test).

Patch SLAs: Critical CVE (CVSS ≥ 9.0): 24h. High (7.0-8.9): 7 days. Medium (4.0-6.9): 30 days. Low (< 4.0): quarterly. Elasticsearch CVEs: tracked separately — any ES CVE requires review by Platform Engineering within 48h regardless of severity.

text:
APACHE KAFKA ARCHITECTURE AND CONFIGURATION REFERENCE v1.8

1. CLUSTER TOPOLOGY
Kafka cluster: 3 brokers (kafka-01, kafka-02, kafka-03) on dedicated VMs (VMware vSphere, VLAN 200). Hardware: 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 2x 4 TB NVMe (Kafka log directories). OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. Kafka version: 3.7.0 (KRaft mode — ZooKeeper removed). Kraft controller: embedded in all 3 brokers (combined broker+controller mode). Replication: RF=3 for all production topics (no data loss if 1 broker fails). Retention: default 7 days for raw event topics; 30 days for audit topics.

2. TOPIC CATALOG
apex.transactions.raw: Partitions 12, RF=3, retention 7d. Producer: ApexPay transaction API (1 producer per AZ). Consumer groups: logstash-txn-pipeline (3 consumers, 1 per partition shard), afds-realtime-scoring (6 consumers). Max message size: 1 MB. Compression: LZ4. Estimated volume: 200K events/day (~2 KB/event = 400 MB/day raw). Key: transaction_id. Offsets: 14-day retention.

apex.iot.telemetry.raw: Partitions 6, RF=3, retention 14d. Producer: MQTT-Kafka bridge (Mosquitto bridge plugin). Consumer groups: logstash-iot-pipeline. Max message size: 64 KB (sensor reading JSON). Compression: Snappy. Estimated volume: 3,600 events/day. Key: asset_id (ensures all readings from same asset go to same partition for ordered processing).

apex.interactions.raw: Partitions 8, RF=3, retention 7d. Producers: CRM webhook, LiveChat export, Email NLP service. Consumer groups: logstash-int-pipeline. Key: customer_id. Max message size: 512 KB (for email body content).

apex.itknowledge.raw: Partitions 4, RF=3, retention 14d. Producers: ServiceNow REST poller, Confluence crawler, SharePoint crawler. Consumer groups: logstash-itkb-pipeline. Key: doc_id. Compression: GZIP (high text compressibility).

apex.audit.raw: Partitions 4, RF=3, retention 30d. Producer: Elasticsearch audit log forwarder. Consumer groups: elastic-siem-pipeline. Immutable log — compaction disabled.

3. SECURITY CONFIGURATION
Authentication: SASL/SCRAM-SHA-512 for all broker-to-client connections. Certificates: mTLS for inter-broker communication (Vault PKI, 90-day certs). ACLs: per service account, per topic, per operation (PRODUCE/CONSUME/DESCRIBE). ACL managed via Confluent Kafka Admin API + Terraform (all ACLs in code, version-controlled).

4. CONSUMER GROUP MONITORING
Kafka consumer lag monitored via Prometheus JMX exporter + custom lag alerting (Burrow equivalent in Alertmanager). Alert: consumer lag > 10,000 messages on apex.transactions.raw for > 5 minutes → P2 (AFDS scoring falling behind). Consumer group offsets stored in internal Kafka topic __consumer_offsets.

text:
HASHICORP VAULT ARCHITECTURE v2.0

1. VAULT CLUSTER TOPOLOGY
Vault version: 1.15.4 (Vault Enterprise — HS/HA with Integrated Storage)
Deployment: Kubernetes StatefulSet, 5 pods (3 voters + 2 non-voters for read scaling), namespace: vault-system on k8s-infra cluster.
Storage backend: Raft Integrated Storage (replicated across all 5 pods). Raft leader election: automatic. Snapshot: automated every 6h to MinIO S3 (apex-vault-snapshots bucket).
Seal type: AWS KMS auto-unseal (Apex AWS account, eu-central-1 region, dedicated KMS key with CloudTrail logging). Rationale: auto-unseal enables pod restarts without manual unseal ceremony; KMS key access restricted to vault-prod IAM role only.
Root token: generated at initialization, immediately revoked after saving Shamir key shards. Root token can be regenerated with quorum of 3/5 Shamir shards (held by: CISO, CTO, VP Platform Engineering, Head of Security, external escrow notaire).

2. SECRETS ENGINES IN USE
KV v2 (apex-kv/): Static secrets — service configurations, third-party API keys, non-rotatable credentials. Path: apex-kv/elasticsearch/api-keys/. All secrets versioned; old versions retained 10 versions.
PKI (apex-pki/): Certificate authority for internal certificates. Sub-paths:
  apex-pki/infrastructure/ — ES node certificates (90d TTL), Logstash TLS certs (90d)
  apex-pki/services/ — service-to-service mTLS certificates (24h TTL, auto-renewed via Vault Agent)
  apex-pki/kubernetes/ — Kubernetes admission webhook TLS (30d TTL)
Database (apex-db/): Dynamic credentials for PostgreSQL (financial system of record). Credentials auto-expire after 1h; lease renewable up to 24h. No stored static passwords.
Elasticsearch (apex-es/): Dynamic API key generation for Elasticsearch. Vault generates ES API keys on-demand with configurable role mapping, TTL 90 days, auto-revocation on lease expiry.
Transit (apex-transit/): Encryption as a service for PII fields before storage. Used by: AFDS to encrypt fraud investigation notes; Pharma batch import service for chemical parameter encryption at rest (beyond ES TLS).
TOTP (apex-totp/): MFA TOTP seed management for legacy systems not supporting Azure AD MFA.

3. VAULT AGENT SIDECAR (KUBERNETES)
Vault Agent injector (Kubernetes mutating webhook) automatically injects Vault Agent sidecars into pods with annotation vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true". The sidecar: authenticates to Vault using Kubernetes service account token (Kubernetes auth method); fetches secrets from designated paths; writes secrets to shared volume as files; renews leases automatically; triggers pod restart if secret cannot be renewed (configurable). All AFDS pods, Logstash pods, and Kafka pods use Vault Agent for API key injection. Zero static secrets in Kubernetes Secrets or ConfigMaps.

doc_title: Apex Fraud Detection System (AFDS) — Technical Architecture v3.0
text:
APEX FRAUD DETECTION SYSTEM (AFDS) — TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE v3.0

1. SYSTEM OVERVIEW
AFDS is the real-time fraud detection and risk scoring system serving all ApexPay transactions, ApexShield insurance claims, and ApexConnect account events. It processes ~200K events/day at peak and must return a risk score within 500ms end-to-end (P99 SLA).

Architecture pattern: Event-driven, Lambda architecture. Real-time layer (speed layer): Kafka consumers + Python scoring service + Elasticsearch feature extraction. Batch layer (accuracy layer): weekly XGBoost model retraining on historical data. Serving layer: Elasticsearch ML inference API for embedding features + Python scoring service for XGBoost inference.

2. COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE
AFDS Kafka Consumer (Python, 6 instances, consumer group afds-realtime-scoring):
Consumes from apex.transactions.raw. For each event: (1) enriches with customer features (point lookup in apex_customer_360 via Elasticsearch GET API, < 5ms); (2) computes velocity counters (Elasticsearch terms aggregation on apex_financial_transactions for customer, device, IP over 1h/24h windows, < 30ms); (3) calls semantic embedding if text field present (Jina v3 inference endpoint, < 50ms); (4) scores with XGBoost model (in-process scikit-learn/xgboost, < 5ms); (5) publishes enriched event with risk_score back to apex_financial_transactions via Elasticsearch bulk API.

XGBoost Model (apex_afds_model_v2.5):
Features (27 total): velocity_last_1h, velocity_last_24h, amount_eur_log, transaction_hour_sin, transaction_hour_cos, ip_country_mismatch, is_new_merchant, geo_distance_from_home, device_type_encoded (5 binary), merchant_category_encoded (8 binary), customer_nps_score, customer_tenure_days, customer_support_tickets_90d, fft_dominant_freq_hz (for IoT-linked transactions), graph_degree_centrality (pre-computed nightly from apex_knowledge_graph), graph_fraud_ring_distance.
Training: 80/20 train/test split, SMOTE oversampling (7% fraud rate → balanced 50% for training), stratified K-fold CV (k=5). Metrics: AUC-ROC 0.973, F1 0.891 (threshold 0.65), Precision 0.94, Recall 0.85.
Deployment: Model artifact stored in MLflow (mlflow.apex.internal). AFDS Python service loads model at startup via mlflow.xgboost.load_model(). Hot reload: new model artifact published to MLflow → Kubernetes Deployment rolling update (zero downtime).

3. ELASTICSEARCH INTEGRATION PATTERNS

Feature extraction query (velocity, executed per transaction):
GET apex_financial_transactions/_search {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"customer_id": "<id>"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-1h"}}}]}}, "aggs": {"velocity_1h": {"value_count": {"field": "transaction_id"}}}, "size": 0}
Latency budget: < 30ms. If > 50ms: use cached value (Redis, 5-minute TTL) and log cache hit.

Risk score write-back (after scoring):
POST apex_financial_transactions/_update/<transaction_id> {"doc": {"afds_score": 0.87, "afds_version": "2.5", "afds_scored_at": "<timestamp>", "afds_top_features": [{"feature": "ip_country_mismatch", "shap": 0.31}, ...]}}
This write-back enables downstream analytics and Agent Builder (Maya) to query pre-scored transactions.

4. FAIL-SAFE BEHAVIOR
Per PLAT-4423 (post INC-0047821): If Elasticsearch is unavailable (cluster health != green OR query latency P99 > 2s for 3 consecutive checks): AFDS switches to rule-based fallback mode (lightweight Python rules: ip_country_mismatch + velocity > 3 + amount > 2000 → flag). Fail-open for transactions < EUR 100; soft-block (3DS challenge) for EUR 100-1000; hard-block for > EUR 1000 in degraded mode.

doc_title: Runbook: Elasticsearch Data Node Recovery (Single Node Failure)
text:
RUNBOOK: ELASTICSEARCH DATA NODE RECOVERY
Version: 2.0 | Applies to: single hot/warm data node failure | Cluster status: YELLOW (primary shards available, replicas on failed node)

STEP 1 — TRIAGE (< 5 min)
Confirm node is actually down (not monitoring agent failure): ping <node-ip> from management VLAN.
Check cluster health: GET /_cluster/health — expect status YELLOW, unassigned_shards > 0.
Identify failed node: GET /_cat/nodes?v — failed node absent from list.
Identify affected shards: GET /_cat/shards?v&h=index,shard,prirep,state,node — unassigned shards listed.

STEP 2 — ASSESS SEVERITY (< 10 min)
If unassigned PRIMARY shards: immediate action required (data unavailable for those shards). Prioritize indices: apex_financial_transactions > apex_customer_360 > apex_security_acls.
If only REPLICA shards unassigned: lower urgency (data available, redundancy reduced). Monitor — ES will auto-reassign replicas if disk space allows. If not auto-reassigning after 5 min: see Step 3.

STEP 3 — MANUAL SHARD ALLOCATION (if auto-allocation stalled)
Check allocation explain: GET /_cluster/allocation/explain — identifies reason for stalled allocation (disk space, tier routing, max_retries exceeded).
If max_retries exceeded: POST /_cluster/reroute?retry_failed — triggers retry of failed allocation attempts.
If disk space issue: identify node with most available disk (GET /_cat/nodes?v&h=name,disk.avail) and manually allocate: POST /_cluster/reroute {"commands": [{"allocate_replica": {"index": "<index>", "shard": 0, "node": "<node>"}}]}.
If tier routing preventing allocation (INC-0052340 scenario): temporarily override: PUT <index>/_settings {"index.routing.allocation.require._tier": null}.

STEP 4 — NODE RECOVERY OR REPLACEMENT
Attempt node restart (ES pod restart): kubectl rollout restart deployment/es-data-<node> -n elastic.
If hardware failure: provision replacement node from infra team (SLA: 48h for new VM). While waiting: temporarily increase replica count on other nodes to restore redundancy.

STEP 5 — VERIFY RECOVERY
GET /_cluster/health — wait for GREEN status.
GET /_cat/indices?v&h=index,health — all indices GREEN.
Run smoke test: python3 /opt/apex/scripts/es/smoke_test_search.py --all-indices.
Update incident ticket with resolution notes.

doc_title: Runbook: Logstash Pipeline Recovery and DLQ Replay
text:
RUNBOOK: LOGSTASH PIPELINE RECOVERY AND DLQ REPLAY
Version: 1.3 | Applies to: any Logstash pipeline failure | Last updated: post INC-0052001

SYMPTOM IDENTIFICATION
Logstash pipeline stopped: zero throughput on Kibana dashboard, pipeline health red.
DLQ accumulation: logstash_pipeline_dlq_events_count > 0 and growing.
High error rate: logstash_pipeline_events_in minus logstash_pipeline_events_out > 5% sustained.

STEP 1 — IDENTIFY FAILED PIPELINE
kubectl get pods -n logstash — identify unhealthy pods.
kubectl logs <pod> -n logstash --tail=100 — look for filter plugin exceptions, ES connection errors, schema validation failures.
Common error patterns:
  - "Elasticsearch::Transport::Error: [400] rejected..." → ES bulk rejected (disk full, mapping conflict)
  - "LogStash::PluginLoadingError" → Logstash plugin crash (usually bad filter config)
  - "Codec::JSON::ParserError" → malformed JSON in Kafka message (DLQ case)

STEP 2 — FIX ROOT CAUSE BEFORE RESTART
Schema issue: Update grok pattern or JSON filter. Test with logstash --config.test_and_exit before deploying. Deploy via ArgoCD (git commit + sync).
ES connection issue: Check ES cluster health. If ES unavailable, wait for ES recovery before restarting Logstash (pipeline will buffer in Kafka — 7-day retention is your buffer).
Disk full: Free disk space on ES nodes (delete warm/cold index snapshots if needed). Then restart pipeline.

STEP 3 — DLQ REPLAY
DLQ location: /var/logstash/dlq/<pipeline_id>/
Check DLQ size: du -sh /var/logstash/dlq/iot-pipeline/
Replay DLQ events (after fixing root cause): Enable DLQ input in pipeline config: input { dead_letter_queue { path => "/var/logstash/dlq" commit_offsets => true pipeline_id => "iot-pipeline" } }. Deploy and monitor: events should drain from DLQ and index successfully. Disable DLQ input and redeploy normal config after DLQ is empty.

STEP 4 — VERIFY
Check pipeline throughput returns to baseline (Kibana dashboard: Logstash Pipelines).
Check DLQ depth: GET http://logstash:9600/_node/stats/pipelines — dlq.queue_size_in_bytes should be 0.
Verify target index document count growing normally.

Check related alerts in PagerDuty for correlated incidents.

doc_title: How-To: Writing Efficient Elasticsearch Queries for Apex Indices
text:
HOW-TO: EFFICIENT ELASTICSEARCH QUERIES FOR APEX INDICES

TARGET AUDIENCE: Data Scientists, Application Developers, Analytics Engineers

1. QUERY PERFORMANCE FUNDAMENTALS

The single most important concept: Elasticsearch filters are cached, queries are not. Structure every query with a bool filter for high-cardinality selective conditions (customer_id, transaction_id, asset_id) and move scoring conditions to the bool query section only when relevance ranking is needed.

WRONG (forces full scoring on every document):
GET apex_financial_transactions/_search {"query": {"match": {"customer_id": "CUST-000042"}}}

RIGHT (uses filter cache):
GET apex_financial_transactions/_search {"query": {"bool": {"filter": [{"term": {"customer_id": "CUST-000042"}}]}}}

Performance impact: Filter query on customer_id in apex_financial_transactions: ~3ms. Match query (scoring): ~45ms. Factor: 15x. At 200K daily transactions, this is the difference between 600s and 9,000s of cumulative query time per day.

2. AGGREGATION BEST PRACTICES
Always set explicit size on terms aggregations (no unbounded cardinality). apex_financial_transactions.device_id has ~340K unique values — terms aggregation without size will attempt to load all of them (INC-0047821 root cause).

WRONG: {"aggs": {"by_device": {"terms": {"field": "device_id"}}}}
RIGHT: {"aggs": {"by_device": {"terms": {"field": "device_id", "size": 100}}}}

For large cardinality counting (unique devices, unique customers), use cardinality aggregation (HyperLogLog++, approximate but fast):
{"aggs": {"unique_customers": {"cardinality": {"field": "customer_id", "precision_threshold": 1000}}}}

3. PAGINATION AT SCALE
NEVER use from+size for deep pagination (e.g. from: 10000 — loads 10,000 docs into memory per shard before discarding). Use search_after for cursor-based pagination or scroll API for export jobs. Example search_after:
GET apex_financial_transactions/_search {"sort": [{"@timestamp": "desc"}, {"transaction_id": "asc"}], "search_after": ["2024-11-01T12:00:00Z", "TXN-001234"], "size": 1000}

4. INDEX-SPECIFIC QUERY TIPS
apex_operational_telemetry: Always filter by asset_id first, then by @timestamp range. The index is sorted by @timestamp; filter on asset_id + date range is extremely efficient.
apex_knowledge_graph: Filter by node_type or edge_type first (low cardinality). Avoid wildcard queries on label field.
apex_customer_interactions: Use semantic query (not match) on the text field for conceptual search. Use match on transcript_text for exact keyword search. Combine with bool filter on customer_id for customer-specific semantic search.

text:
HOW-TO: MULTILINGUAL HYBRID SEARCH ON APEX ELASTICSEARCH

TARGET AUDIENCE: Data Scientists and Application Developers building search features on top of Apex indices.

STEP 1 — CHOOSE YOUR INFERENCE MODEL
The choice depends on your index and use case:
- apex_customer_interactions, apex_pharma_batches: Use .multilingual-e5-small (built-in, zero config, fast)
- apex_policy_vault, apex_technical_docs, apex_it_knowledge_base, apex_unstructured_vault: Use jina-v3-multilingual (better quality, especially cross-lingual)
- apex_multimodal_assets (image + text): Use jina-clip-v2 (only for multimodal use cases)

STEP 2 — CONSTRUCT THE HYBRID SEARCH QUERY (RRF)
Hybrid search combining BM25 (keyword) + kNN (semantic) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion:
GET apex_it_knowledge_base/_search
{
  "retriever": {
    "rrf": {
      "retrievers": [
        {"standard": {"query": {"multi_match": {"query": "elasticsearch heap memory JVM", "fields": ["text^2", "doc_title"], "type": "best_fields"}}}},
        {"knn": {"field": "text", "query_vector_builder": {"text_embedding": {"model_id": "jina-v3-multilingual", "model_text": "elasticsearch heap memory JVM"}}, "num_candidates": 100, "k": 20}}
      ],
      "rank_window_size": 100,
      "rank_constant": 60
    }
  },
  "highlight": {"fields": {"text": {"number_of_fragments": 3, "fragment_size": 200}}},
  "_source": ["doc_id", "doc_title", "source_system", "doc_type", "chunk_index"],
  "size": 10
}

STEP 3 — FILTER BEFORE HYBRID SEARCH
For better performance and precision, add pre-filters inside the standard retriever. Example: search only ServiceNow incidents:
{"standard": {"query": {"bool": {"must": {"multi_match": {...}}, "filter": [{"term": {"source_system": "ServiceNow"}}, {"term": {"doc_type": "incident"}}]}}}}

STEP 4 — CROSS-LINGUAL SEARCH EXAMPLE
Jina v3 and E5-small both support cross-lingual zero-shot retrieval. A query in English will return relevant results from German/French/Italian documents and vice versa. Example: query "Betrugserkennungssystem Ausfall" (DE: "fraud detection system failure") will return English incident reports about AFDS outages with high similarity scores.

STEP 5 — PAGINATION AND RESULT RENDERING
Use search_after with the _id and _score for cursor-based pagination. Always return the chunk_id and doc_id fields — use doc_id to fetch all sibling chunks for full document context (GET apex_it_knowledge_base/_search {"query": {"term": {"doc_id": "SN-INC-0047821"}}}).

doc_title: Politica di Sicurezza IT — Accesso ai Dati Elasticsearch e Gestione delle Credenziali
text:
POLITICA DI SICUREZZA IT — PIATTAFORMA ELASTICSEARCH
Ambito: Entita italiane Apex Conglomerate | Riferimento normativo: GDPR Art. 32, D.Lgs. 231/2001, ACN Framework Nazionale Cybersecurity
Approvata da: CISO, Responsabile Protezione Dati, Direttore Tecnico

1. PRINCIPI DI ACCESSO AI DATI
Tutti gli accessi alla piattaforma Elasticsearch (es-prod) devono rispettare il principio del minimo privilegio (least privilege). Ogni ruolo tecnico ha accesso esclusivamente agli indici e ai campi necessari per le proprie mansioni. Il controllo degli accessi e implementato a livello documentale (Document-Level Security - DLS) e di campo (Field-Level Security - FLS) tramite la configurazione in apex_security_acls.

Autenticazione: Esclusivamente tramite chiavi API individuali (nessuna credenziale condivisa). Le chiavi API hanno validita massima di 90 giorni e sono gestite tramite HashiCorp Vault. L'accesso umano a Kibana avviene tramite SSO Azure Active Directory con MFA obbligatorio.

2. OBBLIGHI DI REGISTRAZIONE E AUDIT
Tutti gli accessi a indici contenenti dati personali (apex_customer_360, apex_financial_transactions, apex_customer_interactions) sono registrati nel log di audit di Elasticsearch. I log vengono archiviati per 3 anni in formato immodificabile su MinIO S3 (sede di Frankfurt) e sono accessibili esclusivamente tramite il ruolo ROLE-AUDIT in apex_security_acls.

3. SEGNALAZIONE DEGLI INCIDENTI DI SICUREZZA
Gli incidenti di sicurezza informatica devono essere segnalati al CISO entro 1 ora dalla rilevazione. Gli incidenti con possibile impatto sulla protezione dei dati personali devono essere valutati per la notifica all'Autorita Garante (Garante Privacy) entro 72 ore ai sensi dell'Art. 33 GDPR. Per incidenti rilevanti ai sensi del D.Lgs. 231/2001, e obbligatoria la segnalazione all'Organismo di Vigilanza entro 48 ore.

ELASTICSEARCH PLATTFORMARCHITEKTUR — MANAGEMENT-ZUSAMMENFASSUNG
Berichtet an: CTO, CIO, CISO | Erstellungsdatum: Q4 2024 | Verteiler: Deutsches IT-Management

UEBERBLICK
Die Apex Elasticsearch-Plattform ist das zentrale Such- und KI-Inference-System der Apex Conglomerate GmbH und ihrer deutschen Tochtergesellschaften. Sie verarbeitet taeglich bis zu 2,4 Millionen Ereignisse aus fuenf Quellsystemen (ApexPay-Transaktionsverarbeitung, IoT-Sensoren, Kundenkommunikation, IT-Wissensdatenbank, Pharmabatch-Qualitaetskontrolle) und stellt die Grundlage fuer das Betrugserkennungssystem AFDS sowie den KI-Agenten Maya dar.

DATENSCHUTZKONFORME ARCHITEKTUR
Die Plattform wurde von Grund auf fuer die Anforderungen der DSGVO konzipiert: Alle Daten verbleiben im Apex-eigenen Rechenzentrum Frankfurt (kein Public-Cloud-Einsatz fuer Personendaten). Technische Datenschutzmassnahmen umfassen: Document-Level Security (DLS) — Nutzer sehen ausschliesslich die ihnen bestimmungsgemass zugaenglichen Dokumente; Field-Level Security (FLS) — personenbezogene Felder werden je nach Rolle ausgeblendet; Verschluesselung aller Daten in Ubertragung und Ruhelage (TLS 1.3, AES-256); Audit-Protokollierung aller Datenzugriffe fuer 3 Jahre.

text:
ARCHITECTURE PLATEFORME ELASTICSEARCH — SYNTHESE DIRECTION IT FRANCE
Destinataires: DSI, RSSI, DPO | Date: Q4 2024 | Classement: Confidentiel Interne

CONTEXTE ET OBJECTIFS
La plateforme Elasticsearch d'Apex constitue le coeur du systeme de detection de fraude (AFDS) et du moteur de recherche semantique utilise par l'agent IA Maya. Elle est deployee exclusivement dans le datacenter de Francfort (Allemagne) afin de garantir la souverainete des donnees sur le territoire de l'Union Europeenne, conformement aux exigences du RGPD et aux recommandations de la CNIL.

CONFORMITE RGPD ET SECURITE
La plateforme met en oeuvre les mesures techniques et organisationnelles requises par l'Article 32 du RGPD. Les principales mesures de securite sont: (1) Chiffrement des donnees en transit (TLS 1.3 exclusivement) et au repos (AES-256); (2) Controle d'acces granulaire par document (DLS) et par champ (FLS) — chaque utilisateur acced uniquement aux donnees necessaires a ses fonctions; (3) Journalisation complete de tous les acces aux donnees personnelles, conservee 3 ans en format immuable; (4) Gestion des secrets via HashiCorp Vault avec rotation automatique toutes les 90 jours.
